It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. You will see which techniques pay off on each architecture, why some help one and hurt the other, and how to measure the effect of every change in time, registers, and LDS, so you can apply the same approach to your own kernels. This is Part 1 of a two-part series. Part 2 will port the final kernel from this post to FP8 on RDNA 4.
